title: Confessions: true or false?
instructions: Decide whether each statement matches the Act.

items.statement: No confession made to a police-officer shall be proved as against a person accused of any offence (s.25).
items.explanation: This is the text of s.25.

items.statement: A confession in police custody is always admissible if the accused signs it.
items.explanation: s.26 requires the immediate presence of a Magistrate.

items.statement: An inducement, threat or promise must have reference to the charge for s.24 to apply.
items.explanation: s.24 requires reference to the charge against the accused.

title: Burden of proof: true or false?
instructions: Decide whether each statement matches the Act.

items.statement: The burden lies on the person who would fail if no evidence were given on either side (s.102).
A fact especially within a person's knowledge must always be proved by the other side.
items.explanation: s.106 puts that burden on the person with the knowledge.

title: Match the legal term
instructions: Match each provision to its effect.

pairs.right: Confession to a police-officer cannot be proved against the accused
Statement as to cause of death can be relevant
Burden on the person with special knowledge
Estoppel by declaration, act or omission

title: Fill in the missing word
instructions: Pick the word that completes the text of the Act.

items.prompt: No confession made to a police-officer shall be ____ as against a person accused of any offence.
When any fact is especially within the ____ of any person, the burden of proving that fact is upon him.

title: Identify the relevant section
instructions: Read the situation and choose the section.

items.scenario: A tells the police, in custody, that he committed the theft. Which section bars proving this against A?
A falsely and intentionally leads B to believe land is A's, and B buys it. Which doctrine stops A denying that later?
A is charged with travelling on a railway without a ticket. Whether he had a ticket is a fact especially within his knowledge.
items.question: On whom does the burden of proving he had a ticket lie?
items.explanation: s.106 illustration (b): the burden is on him.
